units.en: He often took as principle: "Lead only with punishments and people stay out of trouble but feel no shame."
units.literal: He constantly took as principle "If you regulate them with punishments, the people avoid them but have no sense of shame."

units.zh: 吏人有過，但用蒲鞭罰之，示辱而已，終不加苦。
units.en: For minor faults he swatted offenders with a soft rattan whip—enough to shame them, never to injure.
units.literal: When clerks and people had faults, he only used a rattan whip to punish them—displaying shame only—in the end did not add suffering.

units.zh: 事有功善，推之自下。
units.en: When something went well he credited his subordinates.
units.literal: When affairs had merit and goodness, he pushed them from below.

units.zh: 災異或見，引躬克責。
units.en: When omens appeared he blamed himself first.
units.literal: When disasters or prodigies sometimes appeared, he drew himself in and overcame with self-blame.

units.zh: 每行縣止息亭傳，輒引學官祭酒及處士諸生執經對講。
units.en: Touring his counties he halted at post stations and convened local scholars and students for classical discussion.
units.literal: Whenever traveling counties he stopped to rest at courier stations—always summoned education officials, libationers, and recluses and students holding classics to face one another in lecture.

units.zh: 見父老慰以農裏之言，少年勉以孝悌之訓。
units.en: He urged elders with talk of farming and instructed youths in filial piety and brotherly duty.
units.literal: Seeing elders he consoled them with words of farming hamlets; to youths he exhorted with teachings of filiality and fraternal duty.

units.zh: 人感德興行，日有所化。
units.en: Moved by his virtue, people improved day by day.
units.literal: People felt virtue and arose in conduct; daily there was transformation.

units.zh: 靈帝初，征拜太中大夫，傳講華光殿。
units.en: Early in Emperor Ling's reign he became Grand Counselor of the Palace and lectured on the classics at Huaguang Hall.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ling he was summoned and appointed Grand Counselor of the Palace; lectured by transmission at Huaguang Hall.

units.zh: 遷侍中，賜衣一襲。
units.en: Promoted to Palace Attendant and gifted a full set of robes.
units.literal: Promoted to Palace Attendant; granted one suit of clothes.

units.zh: 轉屯騎校尉，遷宗正，轉光祿勛。
units.en: He rotated through Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, and Chamberlain for Palace Attendants.
units.literal: Transferred to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry; promoted to Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan; transferred to Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues.

units.zh: 熹平五年，代許訓為太尉。
units.en: In Xiping 5 he succeeded Xu Xun as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Xiping he replaced Xu Xun as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 靈帝頗好學藝，每引見寬，常令講經。
units.en: Emperor Ling loved scholarship and often summoned Liu Kuan to expound the canon.
units.literal: Emperor Ling rather liked learning and arts; whenever summoning audience with Kuan he regularly ordered him to expound the classics.

units.zh: 寬嘗於坐被酒睡伏。
units.en: Once during an audience he nodded off drunk.
units.literal: Kuan once at sitting was soaked with wine and slept prone.

units.zh: 帝問：『太尉醉邪？』
units.en: The emperor asked whether the Grand Commandant was drunk.
units.literal: The emperor asked, "Is the Grand Commandant drunk?"

units.zh: 寬仰對曰：『臣不敢醉，但任重責大，憂心如醉。』
units.en: Liu answered, "I am not drunk—but my burden weighs so heavily that worry feels like wine."
units.literal: Kuan looked up and replied, "Your servant does not dare be drunk; only the burden is heavy and responsibility great—worry is like drunkenness."

units.zh: 帝重其言。
units.en: The emperor respected his candor.
units.literal: The emperor valued his words.

units.zh: 寬簡略嗜酒，不好盥浴，京師以為諺。
units.en: Liu lived plainly, loved wine, and seldom bathed—the capital turned those habits into jokes.
units.literal: Kuan was plain and negligent and fond of wine; did not like washing or bathing—capital took it as proverb.

units.zh: 嘗坐客，遣蒼頭市酒，迂久，大醉而還。
units.en: Once when hosting guests he sent a servant for wine; the man returned late and roaring drunk.
units.literal: Once entertaining guests he sent a gray-haired servant to buy wine; after a long delay very drunk he returned.

units.zh: 客不堪之，罵曰：『畜產。』
units.en: The guests lost patience and shouted "beast!"
units.literal: Guests could not endure it; they cursed saying, "Livestock."

units.zh: 寬須臾遣人視奴，疑必自殺。
units.en: Liu immediately sent someone to check on the servant, fearing he might harm himself.
units.literal: Kuan shortly sent someone to look at the slave—suspecting he must kill himself.

units.zh: 顧左右曰：『此人也，罵言畜產，辱熟甚焉！
units.en: Turning to his attendants he said, "They insulted a fellow human by calling him cattle—that wound cuts deep.
units.literal: Looking to left and right he said, "This is a human being—curse words calling him livestock—how extreme the insult!

units.zh: 故吾懼其死也。』
units.en: That is why I feared he might take his own life."
units.literal: Therefore I fear his death."

units.zh: 夫人欲試寬令恚，伺當朝會，裝嚴已訖，使侍婢奉肉羹，翻汙朝衣。
units.en: His wife once tried to provoke him: on a court day, after he had dressed, she had a maid spill stew on his ceremonial robes.
units.literal: His wife wished to test Kuan and make him angry; waiting until court assembly; dressing complete; she ordered a serving maid to bring meat stew—overturning and defiling court robes.

units.zh: 婢遽收之，寬神色不異，乃徐言曰：『羹爛汝手？』
units.en: The maid panicked; Liu's expression never changed as he asked softly whether she had burned her hand.
units.literal: The maid hastily gathered it; Kuan's expression was no different; then slowly said, "Did the stew burn your hand?"

units.zh: 其性度如此。
units.en: Such was his temperament.
units.literal: Such was his nature and degree.

units.zh: 海內稱為長者。
units.en: All the empire honored him as a gentleman of true stature.
units.literal: Within the seas he was called a man of mature virtue.

units.zh: 後以日食策免。
units.en: Later a solar eclipse prompted his dismissal.
units.literal: Later owing to solar eclipse he was dismissed by edict.

units.zh: 拜衛尉。
units.en: He was appointed Commandant of the Guards.
units.literal: Appointed Commandant of the Guards.

units.zh: 光和二年，復代段颎為太尉。
units.en: In Guanghe 2 he again succeeded Duan Jiong as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the second year of Guanghe again replaced Duan Jiong as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 在職三年，以日變免。
units.en: After three years another celestial anomaly cost him the post.
units.literal: In office three years; owing to solar anomaly dismissed.

units.zh: 又拜永樂少府，遷光祿勛。
units.en: He then served as Privy Treasurer of Yongle Palace and again as Chamberlain for Palace Attendants.
units.literal: Again appointed Privy Treasurer of Yongle; promoted to Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues.

units.zh: 以先策黃巾逆謀，以事上聞，封逯鄉侯六百戶。
units.en: For having anticipated the Yellow Turban plot and reported it, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lu township with six hundred households.
units.literal: Because beforehand he had planned against Yellow Turban rebellion—reported the affair upward—enfeoffed Marquis of Lu township with six hundred households.

units.zh: 中平二年卒，時年六十六。
units.en: He died in Zhongping 2 at sixty-six.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongping he died; at that time aged sixty-six.

units.zh: 贈車騎將軍印綬，位特進，謚曰昭烈侯。
units.en: The court posthumously honored him as General of Chariots and Cavalry with advanced rank and the title Marquis Brilliant and Stern.
units.literal: Posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry seal and ribbon; rank specially advanced; posthumous title Marquis Brilliant and Severe.

units.zh: 子松嗣，官至宗正。
units.en: His son Liu Song inherited the title and rose to Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan.
units.literal: Son Song succeeded; office reached Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan.

units.zh: 贊曰：卓、魯款款，情愨德滿。
units.en: The historian praises Zhuo Mao and Lu Gong for their steadfast sincerity and overflowing virtue.
units.literal: The eulogy says: Zhuo and Lu were earnest and sincere—emotion sincere, virtue full.

units.zh: 仁感昆蟲，愛及胎卵。
units.en: Their benevolence touched even insects and spared creatures in the egg.
units.literal: Humane influence moved insects; love reached embryos and eggs.

units.zh: 寬、霸臨政，亦稱優緩。
units.en: Liu Kuan and Wei Ba governed with the same gentle forbearance.
units.literal: Kuan and Ba facing governance likewise were called lenient and slow.

units.zh: 獨與司徒袁安同心畢力，持重處正，鯁言直議，無所回隱，語在《袁安傳》。
units.en: He alone, with Minister of Education Yuan An, held the line with unwavering resolve, spoke plainly without hedging—the full account is in the 《Biography of Yuan An》.
units.literal: He alone with Minister of Education Yuan An joined hearts and exhausted strength, held steady and stood upright, spoke bluntly and debated directly, without any evasion; the words are in the 《Biography of Yuan An》.

units.zh: 和帝即位，大將軍竇憲秉權，專作威福，內外朝臣莫不震懾。
units.en: When Emperor He came to the throne, Grand General Dou Xian dominated the government, throwing his weight about until ministers at court and in the provinces quailed before him.
units.literal: When the He Emperor ascended the throne, Grand General Dou Xian grasped power, monopolized authority and favor, and inner and outer court ministers were without exception awed.

units.zh: 宣罷數歲，諫大夫鮑宣數薦宣。
units.en: Some years after Peng Xuan retired, Remonstrance Grandee Bao Xuan repeatedly recommended him to the throne.
units.literal: After Xuan was dismissed several years, remonstrance grandee Bao Xuan repeatedly recommended Xuan.

units.zh: 會元壽元年正月朔日蝕，鮑宣復言，上乃召宣為光祿大夫，遷御史大夫，轉為大司空，封長平侯。
units.en: At the solar eclipse on the new moon of the first month of the first year of Yuanshou, Bao Xuan spoke again; the emperor recalled Peng Xuan as Imperial Household Grandee, then promoted him to commandant of the imperial counselors, grand minister of works, and Marquis of Changping.
units.literal: It happened in the first year of Yuanshou, first month new moon solar eclipse; Bao Xuan again spoke; the sovereign then summoned Xuan as Imperial Household Grandee, promoted commandant of the imperial counselors, transferred to grand minister of works, enfeoffed Marquis of Changping.

units.zh: 黄香字文强，江夏安陆人也。
units.en: Huang Xiang, called Wenqiang, came from Anlu in Jiangxia.
units.literal: Huang Xiang, courtesy name Wenqiang, was a native of Anlu in Jiangxia.

units.zh: 遂博学经典，究精道术，能文章，京师号曰“天下无双江夏黄童”。
units.en: He went on to master the canon and Daoist arts and to write brilliantly; the capital nicknamed him "the unrivaled Huang boy of Jiangxia."
units.literal: Thereupon he became broadly learned in the classics, mastered techniques of the Way, and could compose; the capital dubbed him "the matchless lad of Jiangxia, Huang."

units.zh: 臣香小丑，少为诸生，典郡从政，固非所堪。
units.en: I am a nobody who once merely studied; commanding a commandery is beyond my strength.
units.literal: Your servant Xiang is a petty man, formerly only a student; to administer a commandery and govern is truly beyond what I can bear.

units.zh: 香后告休，及归京师，时千乘王冠，帝会中山邸，乃诏香殿下，顾谓诸王曰：“此‘天下无双江夏黄童’者也。
units.en: After he took leave and came back to Luoyang, the heir of Qiansheng was capped; at the Zhongshan hostel the emperor gathered the princes, called Huang Xiang forward, and told them: "Here is your 'matchless Huang lad of Jiangxia.'"
units.literal: Later he requested leave and returned to the capital; when the Prince of Qiansheng received his cap, the emperor met the princes at the Zhongshan lodge and summoned Huang Xiang below the hall, saying to the kings: "This is the man called 'the matchless lad of Jiangxia, Huang.'"

units.zh: 初除郎中，元和元年，肃宗诏香诣东观，读所未尝见书。
units.en: His first post was gentleman; in Yuanhe 1 Emperor Zhang sent him to the Eastern Pavilion to devour texts he had never opened.
units.literal: First appointed gentleman; in the first Yuanhe year Emperor Zhang ordered Huang Xiang to the Eastern Lodge to read books he had never seen.

units.zh: 后召诣安福殿言政事，拜尚书郎，数陈得失，赏赉增加。
units.en: He was next called to Anfu Hall for statecraft debates, made a Masters of Writing gentleman, spoke bluntly on policy, and watched stipends swell.
units.literal: Later he was summoned to Anfu Hall to discuss policy; appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; repeatedly laid out gains and losses; rewards grew.

units.zh: 六年，累迁尚书令。
units.en: By year six he had climbed to Prefect of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Sixth year: cumulatively promoted to Prefect of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 所著贼、笺、奏、书、令、凡五篇。
units.en: He left five pieces: fu, memoranda, memorials, letters, and orders.
units.literal: His writings—fu, notes, memorials, letters, directives—five pieces in all.

units.zh: 后以为东郡太守，香上疏让曰：“臣江淮孤贱，愚驽小生，经学行能，无可算录。
units.en: Named Dong commandery administrator, he memorialized to refuse: "I am a nobody from the Yangzi-Huai region, a dull young student with no record of learning or conduct worth citing."
units.literal: Later appointed Administrator of Dong commandery; Huang Xiang submitted a memorial declining: "Your servant is base-born between the Yangzi and Huai, a foolish and slow young student, without measurable achievement in classical learning or conduct."

units.zh: 延平元年，迁魏郡太守。
units.en: Yanping 1 moved him to Wei commandery administrator.
units.literal: First Yanping year: transferred to Administrator of Wei commandery.

units.zh: 香料別據奏，全活甚衆。
units.en: Huang Xiang parsed each dossier and kept countless people alive.
units.literal: Xiang separately weighed the evidence in each memorial and spared very many lives.

units.zh: 每郡国疑罪，辄务求轻科，爱惜人命，每存忧济。
units.en: Whenever a province sent up ambiguous cases he leaned toward lenient clauses, guarding lives and easing distress.
units.literal: Whenever commanderies forwarded doubtful crimes he always sought the lightest statute, cherishing human life and preserving compassionate relief.

units.zh: 永元四年，拜左丞。
units.en: In Yongyuan 4 he became Left Assistant.
units.literal: Fourth Yongyuan year: appointed Left Assistant.

units.zh: 十二年，东平清河奏訞言卿仲辽等，所连及且千人。
units.en: In year twelve Dongping and Qinghe reported charges linking Qing Zhongliao and others until nearly a thousand names tangled in the net.
units.literal: Twelfth year: Dongping and Qinghe submitted accusations concerning Qing Zhongliao and others; those implicated approached a thousand.

units.zh: 年九岁，失母，思慕憔悴，殆不免丧，乡人称其至孝。
units.en: He lost his mother at nine; grief wasted him until mourners feared he would follow her; neighbors praised his utmost filial devotion.
units.literal: At nine he lost his mother; longing wasted him until he barely survived mourning; villagers called him supremely filial.

units.zh: 香家贫，内无仆妾，躬执苦勤，尽心奉养。
units.en: His family was destitute, without maids; he shouldered every hardship himself and nursed his father with utter devotion.
units.literal: The Huang household was poor and kept no servants or concubines; he personally endured bitter labor and devoted himself to supporting his parent.

units.zh: 子琼，自有传。
units.en: His son Huang Qiong receives a separate biography.
units.literal: His son Qiong has his own biography.

units.zh: 年十二，大守刘护闻而召之，署门下孝子，甚见爱敬。
units.en: When he was twelve, Administrator Liu Hu summoned him and named him filial attendant at his residence—everyone cherished him.
units.literal: At age twelve Grand Administrator Liu Hu heard of him and summoned him, appointing him Filial Son under his gate; he was greatly loved and respected.

units.zh: 功满当迁，和帝留，增秩。
units.en: His tour qualified him for advancement, yet Emperor He held him back with a higher stipend.
units.literal: His merit complete, he merited promotion; Emperor He kept him and raised his salary grade.

units.zh: 遭值太平，先人余福，得以弱冠特蒙征用，连阶累任，遂极台阁。
units.en: Living under universal peace on inherited luck, he was plucked while still young, climbed step after step, and ended atop the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Encountering an age of Great Peace and relying on ancestors’ leftover fortune, in weak-cap years he alone received special summons; rank followed rank until he reached the summit of the Terrace offices.

units.zh: 讫无纤介称，报恩效死，诚不意悟。
units.en: I had not a hair’s breadth of achievement; dying for the throne would barely repay it—I never dreamed of such grace.
units.literal: Never had I the slightest merit to record; to repay grace with my life would still fall short—I truly did not expect such favor.

units.zh: 卒被非望，显拜近郡，尊位千里。
units.en: Now I am thrust into honors I never sought—openly named to a neighboring province ruling a thousand li.
units.literal: Suddenly heaped with undeserved honor, plainly appointed to a nearby commandery of thousand-li dignity.

units.zh: 臣闻量能授官，则职无废事；
units.en: They say grant office to fit the man and no portfolio sits idle;
units.literal: Your servant has heard that matching capacity when granting office leaves no duty undone;

units.zh: 因劳施爵，则贤愚得宜。
units.en: award fiefs for real labor and wise and plain men each find their place.
units.literal: granting ranks according to labor keeps worthy and simple in proper balance.

units.zh: 诚恐驽顿，孤忝圣恩。
units.en: I fear my own dullness will only stain heaven’s favor.
units.literal: I truly fear that my dullness and slowness will shame the holy grace.

units.zh: 又惟机密端首，至为尊要，复非臣香所当久奉。
units.en: The nerve center of policy is too august for me to clutch forever.
units.literal: Moreover the pivot of state secrets is supremely exalted and crucial—not something your servant Xiang should long hold.

units.zh: 承诏惊惶，不知所裁。
units.en: The summons leaves me shaking; I cannot choose what to do.
units.literal: Receiving the edict I tremble in panic and know not how to decide.

units.zh: 臣香年在方刚，适可驱使。
units.en: I am still in vigorous mid-life—fit only to run errands.
units.literal: Your servant Xiang’s years stand in their prime—just fit to be driven on errands.

units.zh: 愿乞余恩，留备冗官，赐以督责小职，任之宫台烦事，以毕臣香蝼蚁小志，诚瞑目至愿，土灰极荣。
units.en: Let me stay a spare hand, give me some nagging clerk’s duty, pile on palace busywork—that would satisfy my insect-small ambition; I could die content; ash on my name would feel like glory.
units.literal: I beg leftover grace: retain me as a supernumerary, assign me a petty supervisory chore, burden me with vexing terrace paperwork so I may fulfill my ant-like ambition—closing my eyes in peace would be my utmost wish; dust and ash would crown my glory.

units.zh: 帝亦惜香干用，久习旧事，复留为尚书令，增秩二千石，赐钱三十万。
units.en: The emperor valued his competence and intimate knowledge of routine, kept him as Prefect of the Masters of Writing, bumped his rank to two thousand shi, and handed him three hundred thousand cash.
units.literal: The emperor also prized Xiang’s capability and long familiarity with precedent; again retained him as Prefect of the Masters of Writing, raised his salary to two thousand shi, and granted three hundred thousand cash.

units.zh: 在位多所荐达，宠遇甚盛，议者讥其过幸。
units.en: He promoted throngs of talent and soaked up favor until gossip called him over-lucky.
units.literal: In office he recommended many men for advancement; favor was extreme; critics mocked his excessive fortune.

units.zh: 香曰：“《田令》‘商者不农’，《王制》‘仕者不耕’，伐冰食禄之人，不与百姓争利。
units.en: Huang Xiang cited 《Field Ordinance》: merchants do not till; 《Royal Regulations》: officers do not hold the plough—salary men must not squeeze the people.
units.literal: Xiang said: 《Field Ordinance》 states "merchants do not farm"; 《Royal Regulations》 states "officeholders do not plough"; men who harvest ice and eat stipends must not vie with commoners for profit.

units.zh: 乃悉以赋人，课令耕种。
units.en: He handed every plot to the people and taxed the harvest fairly.
units.literal: Thereupon he entirely assigned the plots to commoners and assessed them for cultivation.

units.zh: 时被水年肌，乃分奉禄及所得赏赐班赡贫者，于是丰富之家各出义谷，助官禀贷，荒民获全。
units.en: When floods brought lean years he split stipends and gifts to feed the needy; rich families poured charity grain into state relief and refugees lived.
units.literal: When flood seasons brought famine he divided his salary and grants to relieve the poor; wealthy households then contributed righteous grain to supplement official granaries, and starving people survived.

units.zh: 后坐水潦事免，数月，卒于家。
units.en: Flood paperwork cost him his post; months later he died at home.
units.literal: Later dismissed over flood litigation; several months later died at home.

units.zh: 是后遂管枢机，甚见亲重，而香亦夙勤物务，忧公如家。
units.en: From then on he steered the machinery of state and won deep trust; Huang Xiang threw himself into public business and treated the realm like kin.
units.literal: After this he managed the pivot of power and was greatly trusted; Huang Xiang also worked diligently at public affairs and worried for the public as for his own household.

units.zh: 章以眾心不附，遂密謀閉宮門，誅車騎將軍鄧騭兄弟及鄭眾、蔡倫，劫尚書，廢太后於南宮，封帝為遠國王，而立平原王勝。
units.en: Zhou Zhang, finding popular hearts unattached, secretly plotted to shut the palace gates, execute Deng Zhi and his brothers along with Zheng Zhong and Cai Lun, seize the Masters of Writing, depose the empress dowager in the Southern Palace, banish the emperor to a distant kingdom, and enthrone Prince Sheng of Pingyuan.
units.literal: Zhang, because popular hearts did not attach, then secretly plotted to shut the palace gates, execute Chariots-and-Cavalry General Deng Zhi and his brothers along with Zheng Zhong and Cai Lun, seize the Masters of Writing, depose the empress dowager in the Southern Palace, enfeoff the emperor as king of a distant state, and enthrone King of Pingyuan Sheng.

units.zh: 故严君蚩黄霸之术，密人笑卓茂之政，猛既穷矣，而犹或未胜。
units.en: So Lord Yan sneered at Huang Ba’s soft ways, and Mi county mocked Zhuo Mao’s kindness—yet even the harshest rule could not win the day.
units.literal: Hence Lord Yan mocked Huang Ba’s methods, and the people of Mi laughed at Zhuo Mao’s government—severity pushed to the limit still could not prevail.
